finding.message: IRC R302.5.1: a door leads from the garage 'Garage' directly into the sleeping room 'Bedroom 1'. No door construction makes this permissible.
IRC R311.1: the only way out of 'Utility room' is through the garage.
'Powder room' opens directly onto the kitchen 'Kitchen'.
'Study' can only be reached by passing through a more private room; the privacy gradient from the entrance is not monotone.
'Living room' is a common area but is not the centroid of the plan; some other room is more central to the household's spaces.

The shortest way from the entrance to 'Bedroom 1' never passes within a door of a common area - not counting a long passage, which does not put anybody in contact with the room it runs past. A common area that nobody passes will not be used.

The shortest way from the entrance to 'Bedroom 2' never passes within a door of a common area - not counting a long passage, which does not put anybody in contact with the room it runs past. A common area that nobody passes will not be used.
'Bedroom 1' is private but is also a passage: removing it cuts the plan in two, so somebody must walk through it to reach somewhere else.
'Bedroom 2' is private but is also a passage: removing it cuts the plan in two, so somebody must walk through it to reach somewhere else.
'Hall' is longer than fifty feet, past the threshold at which a passage stops reading as a room.
'Stair' does not adjoin a common room. A stair reached only through passages puts the upper floor behind a dead space.
